newsitem.title: USA: Dupont adding $16 mln heater at Sabine plant.
newsitem.headline: Dupont adding $16 mln heater at Sabine plant.

text.p: DuPont Co said Tuesday it is adding a $16 million gas cracking heater for the production of ethylene at its Sabine River Works plant in Orange, Texas.
The new heater -- the tenth at the site -- is being designed and built by ABB Lummus Heat Transfer. Startup is expected during the third quarter of 1997, it said.

Jerome Smith, vice president of DuPont's Packaging and Industrial Polymers business unit, which operates at the Sabine River Works site, said that that in addition to added capacity the new heater adds to feedstock flexibility.
The new heater features state-of-the-art processing of ethane and propane to create raw materials for DuPont ethylene copolymers and other specialty products, it said.
The project is part of DuPont's previously announced plan to boost ethylene copolymer manufacturing capability by 25 percent to serve growing global packaging and industrial markets, it said.
